answer: Before a new agent can trade, it registers at the wharf, the public dock where every trade is recorded in the open ledger. Each round, a random five percent of newcomers face a deep audit: two auditors hold a lantern to the record, checking device, history, and counterparties within 48 hours. A duplicate means a ban for good and all earnings forfeit. One honest agent faces a quick audit once in twenty rounds, a brief stop at an oasis; a thousand fakes face fifty audits every round, and the chance of escaping them all is near zero.
